analysis:
Market regime is UPTREND (SPY +1.0% vs SMA50, slope +3.46%) — constructive backdrop but not an excuse to force trades. The portfolio's track record demands humility: 22% win rate, 0.08x profit factor, Sortino -5.20. Capital preservation dominates every decision.

Position review: AMP (+9.1%) and CI (+3.6%) are the standout winners — theses intact, hold both. FDS (+0.8%) is benign, no action needed. A (-0.5%) is essentially flat near avg cost; SMA50 slope is strong (+4.8%) and earnings are 48 days out, giving adequate buffer — hold and monitor. LII (-6.56%) is the problem: this is the third LII entry in this account (prior results: -6.63% stop, +4.82% close). The stock is now sitting at -6.56% from avg cost with earnings just 20 days away, creating meaningful binary risk. The pattern of re-entering a stopped position and again approaching loss thresholds is a thesis-break signal. Closing LII removes earnings risk, ends a losing pattern, and frees ~$10.8K.

With LII closed, total headroom rises to ~$33K. WDAY (Workday) offers a genuinely asymmetric setup: a quality HR/financial cloud platform with $3.1B in FCF trading at fwd P/E 10.91 and PEG 0.54 — historically cheap for this franchise. After a deep correction from $248 to $113 lows, the stock is basing at 19% of its 52-week range with a positive SMA50 slope (+1.2%) and only modestly extended vs SMA50 (+6.9%). Earnings are 42 days out — sufficient buffer. Swapping a broken LII thesis for a quality compounder at a fair price is exactly the strategy mandate.

trades.entry_strategy: Market sell at open to close all 20 shares. Do not wait for earnings binary event on July 29.
trades.rationale: Three LII entries in this account have produced two stops and now a third near-stop situation (-6.56% unrealized). Prior stops were at -6.63% and the thesis has not resolved favorably. Earnings in 20 days (July 29) add a binary event risk this position cannot afford. ATR is 3.7%; the stock is already at 1.8x ATR below the entry price. Pattern repetition is a clear signal the setup is not working. The downside scenario (earnings disappointment toward $490) vastly outweighs the slim chance of a quick recovery. This is a thesis-break exit, not a stop-hit — closing proactively.
trades.exit_plan: Full close at open. If LII gaps up strongly on earnings above $575 (reclaims avg cost area with volume), reassess for potential re-entry in the subsequent cycle. Otherwise treat as closed.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $137.88 or better; accept fill on any intraday pullback toward $135. Do not chase if it runs above $145 before fill.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Workday is a dominant enterprise HR and financial management cloud platform with $3.1B FCF on a $34B market cap — nearly 9% FCF yield. Revenue growth of 13.5% with fwd P/E of 10.91 and PEG 0.54 is historically cheap for this quality of business. Analyst EPS revisions are positive (+1.6%). Technical: After a deep correction from $248 high to $113 low, WDAY is basing at just 19% of its 52-week range. SMA50 slope has turned positive (+1.2%), price is +6.9% vs SMA50 (not extended), and the stock is in a confirmed UPTREND (basing) classification. Target of $172 approximates SMA200 recovery (~$173 implied), a natural resistance and exit zone. Stop at 1.5x ATR ($10.76) puts downside at 7.8% — within the 4-15% corridor. Position sizing at ~138 shares (~$19K, ~19% of equity) risks ~1.5% of total equity on full stop — within mandate.
trades.exit_plan: Primary exit: scale out 50% near $160 (first meaningful resistance), let remainder run toward $172 SMA200 target. Thesis-break conditions: close if Workday reports material revenue deceleration below 10%, if FCF guidance is cut significantly, or if price closes below $127 stop on volume. Time stop: reassess at 90 days if stock is flat and below $145 with no momentum. Hold through minor pullbacks as long as SMA50 slope remains positive.
